model_answer: Pass@3 is the chance that at least one of three tries passes, so a retrying harness looks good on it. Pass^3 is the chance that all three pass, so it shows how reliable one try is. They disagree because the first grows with retries and the second shrinks. To tell two rates apart I would compare their Wilson intervals and call them different only when the intervals do not overlap.
prompt: Explain why pass@3 and pass^3 can disagree, and how you would tell two pass rates apart.
rubric: Defines pass@k as at least one of k passes and pass^k as all k pass

Compares Wilson intervals, not the point estimates

model_answer: I would run enough trials that the interval around each rate is narrower than the gain, and the width shrinks only with the square root of the trials, so the count can be large. Beyond sampling, infrastructure, time limits and flaky checks make runs differ, and a change that looks like a gain can be one of them.
